chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from al-Asamm, from Misma', from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ruled concerning a penetrating wound that occurs in a limb that its compensation is one-third of the diyah of that limb.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: title of Imam 'Ali عليه السلام in the report
key_terms.النَّافِذَةِ: a penetrating wound passing into or through the limb
key_terms.الْعُضْوِ: the bodily limb or organ that was injured
key_terms.ثُلُثَ الدِّيَةِ: one-third of the prescribed blood-money compensation
key_terms.دِيَةُ ذَلِكَ الْعُضْوِ: the compensation assigned specifically to that limb
key_terms.قَضَى: issued a legal judgment or ruling

ai.seo_question: What is the diyah for a penetrating wound in a limb according to Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a legal ruling attributed to Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام regarding bodily injury compensation. It states that for a penetrating wound in a limb, the compensation is one-third of the diyah assigned to that particular limb.
